questions.stem: Which of the following statements expresses that there is exactly one student in the class with blue eyes?
questions.solution: The uniqueness quantifier (∃!) states that there exists exactly one element with a certain property. Choice B expresses this by saying 'there exists a unique x such that x is a student and has blue eyes.' The other choices either express different properties or are logically incorrect.
questions.explanation: Choice A says all students have blue eyes, not just one. Choice C negates the possibility of two students having blue eyes but doesn't guarantee uniqueness. Choice D states that if someone has blue eyes, there can be no other student, which is too restrictive.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A because it seems to imply that all students have blue eyes, but it does not express the uniqueness of a single student with blue eyes.
